trust_decision.summary: An OCSP BasicOCSPResp is accepted as proof about the queried server certificate on the strength of its signature, optional nonce and single-response count only; the response's CertificateID (issuer name hash + issuer key hash + serial) is never bound to the certificate that was queried, so a valid response about a different certificate is accepted. The decision is made in OcspClient.validateResponse and consumed in OcspServerCertificateValidator.

landing_point.why: It is the only place where a received BasicOCSPResp is turned into a validated result, so 'missing CertificateID validation' maps to this method first.

fix_sites.entry_point: OcspServerCertificateValidator (public handler added to a TLS client pipeline)
OcspServerCertificateValidator (public handler added to a TLS client pipeline)
OcspServerCertificateValidator (public handler added to a TLS client pipeline)
internal HTTP client handler created by OcspClient.query; no public entry point

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The only other OCSP-status consumers are in the example module: a solver can call them demo code whose verify() is the application's own policy hook, and note that they already compare the CertID serial number, so the library's CertID fix looks inapplicable there.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate responses must survive: a responder may answer with a CertID computed under a digest other than the SHA-1 used in the request (the check must recompute with the response's own hash algorithm, as CertificateID.matchesIssuer does), and a response may be signed by a delegated responder certificate chained to the issuer rather than by the issuer itself; a naive fix that rebuilds a SHA-1 CertificateID locally or requires the signer to be the issuer rejects both.

O6_input_shapes: BasicOCSPResp whose CertID serial number differs from the queried certificate
BasicOCSPResp whose CertID issuer name hash / issuer key hash does not match the issuer (same or different serial)
OCSP response whose response object is not a BasicOCSPResp (unknown ResponseBytes OID)
OCSP response with null/unsuccessful response bytes (OCSPException from getResponseObject)
BasicOCSPResp carrying more than one SingleResp
no response at all: channel closed or responder silent (added 10s timeout / channelInactive failure)

O9_family: improper certificate validation (CWE-295): OCSP response not bound to the queried certificate, allowing replay of another certificate's response
